steps.label: Do Now: Bit Strings (2 of 2)
steps.content:
Do Now: Bit Strings (2 of 2)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy must every answer here have exactly 5 bits?Show the answer

Shifts and circulates keep the length of their string, and AND, OR and XOR give a string as long as the longer one.

4 minutes. Every string has 5 bits. Type each answer as 5 bits.

Total: 2 marks

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: shifts and the order

steps.text: A similar question. Work out LCIRC-1 10110. Every bit moves 1 place left.
The left bit (1) falls off. LCIRC is a circulate, so it comes back on the right. A shift would put a 0 there instead.
The order. Work out 11001 XOR 00101 AND 01011. The order is: brackets, NOT, shifts and circulates, AND, XOR, OR. So AND goes first, wherever it is in the line.
AND first: 00101 AND 01011 = 00001. AND gives 1 only where both bits are 1.
Then XOR: 11001 XOR 00001 = 11000. XOR gives 1 where the bits are different. Now do the same with the expressions in your question.

ACSL Junior Contest 2

Contest 2 Revision: Notation and Bit Strings

Competition

Think → Pair → ShareFour of the five contest questions are on these two topics. Why is a quick, sure method worth more than a clever one?Show the answer

Each question has one answer and no part marks, so one slip loses the whole point. A method you can repeat step by step makes slips rare.

  • 1 minutes. Today: the key facts for both topics, then contest questions in a game.
  • In the contest: two questions on prefix, infix and postfix and two on bit-string flicking.

steps.label: Key Facts: Prefix, Infix and Postfix
steps.content:
Key Facts: Prefix, Infix and Postfix

Think → Pair → SharePrefix and postfix use the same stack. What changes between them, and why?Show the answer

The reading direction and the side the first popped value goes on. Prefix puts the operator before its values, so it is read from the other end.

3 minutes. Add anything you had forgotten to your notes.

FormThe operator goesExample
Infixbetween the two values(6 + 2) * 3
Prefixbefore the two values* + 6 2 3
Postfixafter the two values6 2 + 3 *
  • Order in infix: brackets, then ↑ (power), then * and /, then + and -.
  • Two of the same rank: left to right. Two power arrows: right to left.
  • A number next to a letter or a bracket means multiply: 2B is 2 * B.
  • Postfix: read from the left. A number: push it. An operator: pop two, work them out, push the answer. The first value popped goes on the right.
  • Prefix: read from the right, the same stack. The first value popped goes on the left.
  • Infix to prefix or postfix: put brackets round every operation, move each operator to the front (prefix) or the end (postfix) of its brackets, then remove the brackets.

steps.label: Key Facts: Bit-String Flicking
steps.content:
Key Facts: Bit-String Flicking

Think → Pair → ShareWhy can a * in a solve-for-x answer stand for more than one value of x?Show the answer

A * bit can be 0 or 1 and the expression is still true, so each * doubles the number of values the pattern stands for.

3 minutes. Add anything you had forgotten to your notes.

OperatorWhat it does
NOTflips every bit
AND1 only where both bits are 1
OR1 where at least one bit is 1
XOR1 where the two bits are different
LSHIFT-n, RSHIFT-nmove every bit n places; bits fall off and zeros come in
LCIRC-n, RCIRC-nmove every bit n places; bits that fall off come back at the other end
  • The order: brackets, NOT, shifts and circulates, AND, XOR, OR. Two of the same: left to right. A chain like NOT LSHIFT-1: the one next to the bits goes first.
  • Different lengths: pad the shorter string with zeros on the left.
  • Big counts: on 5 bits a circulate of 5 changes nothing, so use only the remainder.
  • Solve for x: go column by column. Write * for a bit that can be 0 or 1. Undo the last operator first.

steps.label: Data Bridge: Use Your Notes
steps.content:
Data Bridge: Use Your Notes

Think → Pair → ShareWhy answer from your notes, and not from memory alone?Show the answer

Checking your notes while you answer fixes a gap before it costs you a point in the contest.

1 minutes.

  1. Open your notes with the pen icon at the top. Keep paper for the stack and the bit columns.
  2. Answer the contest questions on notation and bit strings to earn coins, then build a bridge to get the truck across.
  3. Type bit strings with or without spaces. For solve for x, use * or list every value.
  4. If the bridge breaks, answer new questions to earn coins, then try the same level again.

Each step on paper can be checked. A step done only in your head is easy to slip on and hard to find again.

The order of the two popped values, because a minus or a divide gives a different answer when the two values swap.
